claims.claim: The arbitrary-sharing-number no-teleport problem belongs to NP.
claims.evidence: Let L be the initial number of live feature occurrences. Every non-teleport move has a feature live at both selected tiles and deletes at least those two occurrences, so a successful play has at most floor(L/2) moves. Its tile sequence is therefore polynomial in the explicit input. A verifier can replay each move, require distinct consecutive tiles and a nonempty live intersection, delete all features live at both endpoints, and accept exactly when no occurrence remains. These operations are polynomial-time. Moreover, an unordered tile pair cannot be used legally twice because its first traversal removes every feature then live at both endpoints and deleted occurrences never return.
claims.search_method: Direct decreasing-measure and certificate-verifier proof, supplemented by exact integer-bitmask certificate generation and replay on the bounded test families.

claims.claim: There is an exact characterization by perfect matchings plus an ordered Euler trail with precedence constraints.
claims.evidence: Necessity: the moves deleting a feature f pair all vertices in its support S_f, giving a perfect matching M_f. Every move deletes some feature, and no unordered tile pair can recur, so the move sequence is an Euler trail of the simple union H of the matchings. If an H-edge uv is not in M_f but both endpoints contain f, then f must already be deleted at at least one endpoint, placing that endpoint's M_f-edge earlier. Sufficiency: formally simulate the ordered trail and suppose the earliest scheduled matching incidence m_f(u)=uv fails because an earlier nonmatching edge uw deleted f at u. Since m_f(u) is later, precedence on uw forces m_f(w) before uw. By earliest-failure minimality, m_f(w) successfully deleted f at w, making it impossible for uw subsequently to delete f at u. This contradiction shows every matching incidence succeeds. Hence each H-edge is legal because it belongs to some matching, and all occurrences are deleted. Exact exhaustive comparison with state-space reachability found agreement on all 956 tested instances with n at most 5, at most 3 features, and arbitrary nonempty even supports.
claims.search_method: Independent proof of both directions, followed by exhaustive enumeration of perfect matchings, Euler trails, precedence constraints, and exact live-occurrence reachability.

claims.claim: If every occurring feature appears on exactly two tiles, no-teleport solvability is decidable in linear time even with unbounded sharing number.
claims.evidence: For a feature supported on exactly {u,v}, neither occurrence can be deleted except by transition uv. Thus every feature having that endpoint pair remains live until the first uv traversal, when all such parallel features are deleted together; afterward uv cannot be legal again. Consequently successful plays are exactly Euler trails covering every edge of the simple endpoint graph K. The standard criterion is that its edge-bearing vertices are connected and it has zero or two odd-degree vertices. K can be built in O(L) word-RAM time by scanning the occurrences, compressing nonempty tile identifiers, radix-sorting endpoint pairs, and deduplicating; connectivity and degree parity are then linear. Duplicate endpoint pairs allow unbounded sharing number. Exact reachability and this graph criterion agreed on all 3,527 tested frequency-two instances with n at most 5 and up to 5 features, including duplicates and featureless instances.
claims.search_method: Direct reduction to unused edges of a simple graph, complexity audit of its construction, and exhaustive comparison with exact reachability.

claims.claim: The obvious static relaxation—choosing feature-perfect-matchings whose simple union is Eulerian—is not sufficient.
claims.evidence: The stated five-tile instance is a valid counterexample. Its three two-tile supports force triangle edges 01, 02, and 12. Tiles 3 and 4 each contain only their respective four-support feature, so in any solution they are degree-one trail endpoints. If their matching attachments meet distinct core vertices, the union has four odd vertices; hence both must attach at the same core vertex i. A trail must then go from one leaf through i, traverse the core triangle as a circuit, and finish through i to the other leaf. In the orientation from tile 3, the first triangle edge out of i deletes at i the feature supported on {0,1,2,4}, making the final i-4 move illegal; the reverse orientation symmetrically destroys the {0,1,2,3} feature needed at tile 3. Nevertheless, the exhibited matchings give the connected simple union {01,02,12,03,04}, whose only odd vertices are 3 and 4. Exhaustive state search independently confirmed unsolvability and confirmed that no matching/Euler ordering satisfies the precedence constraints.
claims.witness: Feature supports {0,1}, {0,2}, {1,2}, {0,1,2,3}, and {0,1,2,4}; choose matchings 01, 02, 12, (03,12), and (04,12), respectively. Their simple union is Eulerian, but the Tiles instance has no no-teleport solution.
claims.search_method: Complete degree-parity and trail-order case analysis, plus exhaustive exact state-space and matching/Euler-order search on the concrete instance.

claims.claim: An exact state-space algorithm runs in O(n^2 L·2^L) time and O(n·2^L) space.
claims.evidence: The pair (v,M), consisting of the current tile and the L-bit live-occurrence mask, contains all information relevant to future play. For each of at most n-1 next tiles, an O(L) scan determines the complete live common-feature set; the transition is permitted exactly when that set is nonempty and then deterministically clears both endpoint occurrences for every such feature. Thus the recurrence is exact. Every transition clears at least two bits, so the state graph is acyclic. There are at most n·2^L states and O(nL) work per state, yielding O(n^2 L·2^L) time. One memo table shared by all starting tiles occupies O(n·2^L) space; recursion depth and transition workspace are smaller. The L=0 case is accepted directly. The persisted checker implements these transitions with integer masks and successfully ran the stated exhaustive comparisons.
claims.search_method: State-sufficiency, transition-cost, state-count, and acyclicity proof, accompanied by an executable exact integer-mask implementation.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a full complexity classification for arbitrary sharing number through either a polynomial-time algorithm or a matching hardness result. The draft proves NP membership, an exact ordered-matching characterization, a restricted linear-time case, a counterexample to a weaker relaxation, and an exponential exact algorithm. All are material and survive audit, but none is the requested unrestricted polynomial-time algorithm or hardness result. The final writeup explicitly says that the complete classification remains unresolved and labels the resolution PARTIAL, so it does not overclaim and claimed_resolution is accurate.
checks_performed: Read the exact target and Tiles definitions from only the authorized source JSON and audited only the authorized iteration-4 draft; used no web, retrieval database, treatment receipt, prior run, verification report, or other solution.
